title: How the Go SDK sends ZCC requests and pages v1 and v2 lists

prose.text: Go ZCC services are package functions that take a `*zscaler.Service`. Most go through `NewZccRequestDo`; some reads and deletes use the generic path: [[zcc.sdk-go.legacy-routing:zcc-services-use-generic-path]]. Function names and endpoints are generated: run `node scripts/kb.mjs surface <package>`.

prose.label: The request helper.
prose.text: {{request-do-decodes}} The response it hands back is synthetic: [[shared.sdk-go.request-handling:request-do-fabricates-200]] Methods that pass it pre-marshaled bytes send an empty object: [[shared.sdk-go.request-handling:zcc-request-do-double-marshals]] {{legacy-body-encoded-again}} In legacy mode it routes as described in [[zcc.sdk-go.legacy-routing]].

prose.label: v1 lists.
prose.text: How the v1 helper pages and stops is [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-v1-stops-on-page-shorter-than-requested]] and [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-v1-extra-request]]. {{v1-readallpages}} {{v1-callers}} The forwarding-profile list makes one request: [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-forwarding-profile-single-request]].

prose.label: v2 lists.
prose.text: The v2 query keys and list envelope are [[zcc.api.v2-wire:offset-query]] and [[zcc.api.v2-wire:list-envelope]]. The page size it sends is [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-v2-page-size]]. How the v2 helper advances and stops is in [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-skip-advances-by-requested-size]] and [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-guards-need-envelope-metadata]]; its callers are [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-v2-callers]].

checks.do: Whether a v1 list was drained with `ReadAllPages` or fetched as one page, and whether a v2 list carried paging metadata.
Whether a v2 call was given `page` or `search` keys, which v2 endpoints do not read.

request-do-decodes.statement: `NewZccRequestDo` encodes its options struct as query parameters, JSON-marshals the body, sends the request, and decodes the response body into the target value when one is passed.

v1-readallpages.statement: `common.ReadAllPages` applies any JMESPath filter from the context only after all pages are collected.
v1-readallpages.conditions: Narrowed to the JMESPath fact: the page-size clamp, page-1 start and short-page stop are held by shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-v1-stops-on-page-shorter-than-requested.

v1-callers.statement: The v1 helper backs the Go reads of admin roles, admin users, the fail-open policy, ZDX and ZPA group entitlements, and devices.

device-type-by-name.statement: `common.GetDeviceTypeByName` turns a platform name, in any case, into its number (ios 1, android 2, windows 3, macos 4, linux 5), also accepts the numeric strings 1 to 5, returns 0 with no error for an empty string, and errors on anything else.

common-intorstring.statement: The shared `common.IntOrString` always marshals as a JSON number and decodes a number, a numeric string, null or an empty string (the last two as 0). Its comment says every ZCC write endpoint wants the number, and that quoted integers on the web-policy `/edit` endpoint fail silently with `{"success":"false","id":0}`.

legacy-body-encoded-again.statement: The Go legacy ZCC client also JSON-encodes whatever body it is given, so the four methods that pass an already-marshaled `bytes.Buffer` (admin-user update, both entitlement updates, manage-pass update) send an empty object in legacy mode as well as on the OneAPI path.
legacy-body-encoded-again.conditions: The legacy client encodes with `json.NewEncoder(buf).Encode(body)`, which renders a `*bytes.Buffer` as `{}` like `json.Marshal`; not sent to a tenant.
